title: Dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the dimensions of its local rings
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and for $x\in X$ let $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be its local ring at $x$. Then the Krull dimension $\dim X$ of the underlying topological space of $X$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] equals $\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$, where $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the Krull dimension of the ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and the supremum is taken in $\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ (both sides are $-\infty$ when $X$ is empty).

source.place: Properties, Lemma Tag 04MU (label lemma-dimension, line 1233), equality of (1) and (2); tag verified in stacks-project/tags/tags (04MU,properties-lemma-dimension)

proof.text: For a point $x\in X$, the Krull dimension of the stalk $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the supremum of the lengths of chains of generalizations $x=x_0,\ldots,x_n$ with $x_{i-1}\in\overline{\{x_i\}}$ and $x_{i-1}\ne x_i$ [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains].

source.place: Properties, Lemma Tag 02IZ (properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring), applied to the closure of the point x

proof.text: The assignments $x\mapsto\overline{\{x\}}$ and $Z\mapsto\xi_Z$, where $\xi_Z$ is the unique generic point of an irreducible closed subset $Z$ [lem-sc-scheme-sober], identify points of $X$ with irreducible closed subsets. A singleton is irreducible, and the closure of an irreducible subset is irreducible [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-closure]. Under this identification, $x_{i-1}\in\overline{\{x_i\}}$ with $x_{i-1}\ne x_i$ is equivalent to the strict inclusion $\overline{\{x_{i-1}\}}\subsetneq\overline{\{x_i\}}$: inclusion follows by monotonicity of closure, and equality would contradict the uniqueness of generic points. Conversely, if $Z_{i-1}\subsetneq Z_i$ is a chain of irreducible closed subsets, then their generic points satisfy $\xi_{Z_{i-1}}\in Z_i=\overline{\{\xi_{Z_i}\}}$ and are distinct. Thus chains of generalizations based at any point correspond exactly to chains of irreducible closed subsets of the same length whose first member is the closure of that point.

source.place: Properties, Lemma Tag 04MU (properties-lemma-dimension), equality of (1) and (2), using the generic-point correspondence of Schemes Lemma Tag 01IS

proof.text: By the definition of topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], its value is the supremum of lengths of all chains of irreducible closed subsets. By step 2, every such chain is counted by the generalization-chain supremum for its first generic point, while every generalization chain gives such a closed-subset chain. Step 1 therefore identifies this supremum with $\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$. If $X$ is empty, both suprema are $-\infty$ by the stated conventions; otherwise the same chain correspondence applies, so the equality holds in all cases.
